newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES utility leads Russian shares up.
newsitem.headline: UES utility leads Russian shares up.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday on high interest in national utility Unified Energy System (UES) ahead of a cash auction of 8.5 percent of the company, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.15 percent to 190.79 on $18.74 million in volume.
Bids for the UES auction are accepted until December 23. The price of each shares is 500 roubles (about $0.09).
"There are rumours that a big strategic investor plans to invest in UES through the auction," Boris Shvedsky, a broker at IK Aton, said.
UES ordinary shares rose to $0.0845 from $0.0833 at Tuesday's close. UES preferred were $0.0656 after $0.0650.

Alexei Genkin, manager of international sales at IK Alfa-Capital, said traders expected the potential strategic investor to hold his shares, adding that the UES price was a new benchmark for the paper.
Dmitry Yevenko, chief trader from United City Bank, expected more interest in UES in coming days with profit-taking later.
The news that the Federal Bankruptcy Agency had summoned officials from oil firms NK Sidanko and KomiTEK to discuss their subsidiaries' tax arrears and debts had no impact on the market, Genkin said.
Sidanko subsidiary Kondpetroleum owes 564.2 billion roubles in tax arrears and 227 billion roubles in pension contributions.
"Kondpetroleum shares are highly illiquid," Genkin said. "It has very little downside potential."
Kondpetroleum rose to $1.49 from $1.425 at November 29 close, when the share was last traded.
Genkin said the price was not indicative as only 20,000 Kondpetroleum shares were traded on Wednesday.
He said there was interest in Rostelekom preferred shares as they were undervalued compared to other preferred stocks.
Genkin said he expected a quiet market until the end of the year and a rise after that as fixed-income operators shift funds into shares due to falling yields on the government securities market.
The annualised average yield on an issue of six-month Treasury bills fell to 32.25 percent at an auction on Wednesday from 38.10 percent at the previous auction last week.
Gazprom fell to $0.335 from $0.337, Mosenergo was $0.986 after $0.988, Tatneft fell to $43.00 from $47.97, Sverdlovskenergo was $0.358 after $0.380 on Monday when it was last traded.
